s: This is the default tier, applying to age (Massachusetts Board of Retirement v. Murgia, 1976), disability (Cleburne, 1985), wealth (San Antonio v. Rodriguez, 1973), and most economic classifications.
The classification is valid if it is rationally related to a legitimate government interest.
The challenger must negate "every conceivable basis" that might support it, and the legislature need not articulate its reasons (FCC v. Beach Communications, 1993).
Courts invalidate laws that rest on bare animus toward a politically unpopular group, which is not a legitimate interest.
